root.label: Pointers and arrays
root.note: A pointer value is an address plus a claim about which object it belongs to.

children.label: Pointer values
children.note: Every object pointer value is one of exactly four kinds.

children.label: Past-the-end
children.note: May be formed, copied, compared and subtracted, never dereferenced.

children.label: Invalid
children.note: After storage ends; dereference or delete is UB, any other use is implementation-defined.

children.label: Same address, different value
children.note: p + 1 == &neighbour is unspecified.

children.label: Decay
children.note: Arrays convert to a pointer to their first element in most expressions.

children.label: No decay
children.note: Under sizeof, decltype, typeid, unary &, reference binding and range-for.

children.label: Array parameters
children.note: void f(int a[10]) declares f(int*); the bound is ignored.

children.label: Deduction
children.note: By-value T deduces int*; const T& deduces int[N].

children.label: &a vs a
children.note: &a is int(*)[N]; &a + 1 steps over the whole array.

children.label: Arithmetic
children.note: Defined only within one array, counting one past the end.

children.label: Out of range
children.note: Forming a pointer outside [0, n] is UB even without a dereference.

children.label: ptrdiff_t overflow
children.note: Subtracting across a char array longer than PTRDIFF_MAX is UB.

children.label: Multidimensional
children.note: int m[3][4] is three arrays of four; indexing past a row is UB.

children.label: Byte walking
children.note: Stepping through object bytes is relied on but under-specified; P1839 addresses it.

children.label: Comparison
children.note: == works everywhere; < is only specified within one object.

children.label: Unrelated with <
children.note: Unspecified in C++, undefined in C, never a constant expression.

children.label: Member order
children.note: Later-declared members compare greater; C++23 dropped the same-access condition.

children.label: std::less
children.note: Guarantees an implementation-defined strict total order over pointers.

children.label: Other pointer kinds
children.note: Function pointers, nullptr_t and interconvertible objects follow their own rules.

children.label: Interconvertible
children.note: Standard-layout object and first member, or union and member; other casts only relabel the pointer.

children.label: Function pointers
children.note: No arithmetic; calling through a mismatched type is UB; to void* is conditional.

children.label: std::nullptr_t
children.note: Converts to pointers, not integers; to bool only by direct-initialization.

children.label: References and to_address
children.note: Aliases without object identity, and raw pointers without dereferencing.

children.label: References
children.note: Not objects; may need no storage; never null or reseated in valid code.

children.label: std::to_address
children.note: C++20: raw pointer from a fancy pointer or iterator, safe for end().
